magic_career <- tibble(
  season = c("1979-80", "1980-81", "1981-82", "1982-83", "1983-84", "1984-85",

  ppg = c(18.0, 21.6, 18.6, 16.8, 17.6, 18.3, 18.8, 23.9, 19.6, 22.5, 22.3, 19.4),

  championship = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),

> *"Ask not what your teammates can do for you. Ask what you can do for your teammates."* – Magic Johnson

## The Magical Rookie

On May 16, 1980, a 20-year-old rookie did something that had never been done before and has never been done since. With Kareem Abdul-Jabbar injured and the Lakers' championship hopes in jeopardy, Magic Johnson started at center in Game 6 of the NBA Finals—and scored 42 points, grabbed 15 rebounds, and dished 7 assists.

The Lakers won the championship. Magic won Finals MVP as a rookie. **It was the announcement that basketball had a new kind of leader.**

```{r career-assists, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Magic's assist numbers were unprecedented for a player of his size"

highchart() %>%
  hc_chart(type = "spline") %>%
  hc_title(text = "Magic Johnson: Career Assists Per Game") %>%
  hc_subtitle(text = "Consistently elite playmaking throughout his career") %>%
  hc_xAxis(categories = magic_career$season, labels = list(rotation = -45)) %>%
  hc_yAxis(
    title = list(text = "Assists Per Game"),
    min = 5,
    plotLines = list(list(value = 11.2, color = "#e94560", dashStyle = "dash",
                          label = list(text = "Career Avg: 11.2")))
  ) %>%
  hc_add_series(name = "APG", data = magic_career$apg, color = "#552583") %>%
  hc_add_theme(hc_theme_flatdark())
```

## The Smile That Changed a Team

Magic didn't lead through intimidation or intensity. He led through joy. His smile was contagious, his enthusiasm infectious. He made the game look fun—because for him, it was.

But don't mistake joy for softness. Magic was one of the fiercest competitors in NBA history. He just expressed it differently.

## Making the Team Shine

Magic's career statistics tell only part of the story. The real measure of his impact was what happened to his teammates when they played alongside him.

```{r triple-doubles, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Magic's versatility: scoring, rebounding, AND playmaking"

magic_stats <- tibble(
  stat = c("Points", "Assists", "Rebounds"),
  career = c(19.5, 11.2, 7.2),
  playoff = c(19.5, 12.3, 7.7)
)

highchart() %>%
  hc_chart(type = "bar") %>%
  hc_title(text = "Magic's All-Around Game") %>%
  hc_xAxis(categories = magic_stats$stat) %>%
  hc_add_series(name = "Regular Season", data = magic_stats$career, color = "#552583") %>%
  hc_add_series(name = "Playoffs", data = magic_stats$playoff, color = "#FDB927") %>%
  hc_plotOptions(bar = list(dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{y:.1f}"))) %>%
  hc_add_theme(hc_theme_flatdark())
```

| Achievement | Value |
|------------|-------|
| Career Assists | 10,141 |
| Triple-Doubles | 138 |
| Championships | 5 |
| Finals MVPs | 3 |
| MVP Awards | 3 |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Lessons from Magic's Leadership

1. **Elevate others** - The best leaders make everyone around them better
2. **Joy is contagious** - Positive energy transforms team culture
3. **Versatility wins** - Being able to play any position made Magic invaluable
4. **Rise to the moment** - His Game 6 performance showed what's possible under pressure
:::
